long_biography.plain_text:
Investor Ray Dalio and his son Mark founded OceanX to combine marine science, exploration, education and storytelling. The nonprofit initiative gives scientists access to advanced laboratories and submersibles, while media partnerships turn expedition findings into films and classroom material for audiences beyond the research community.

Its programmes document deep-sea life and give young explorers hands-on experience in ocean science, operations and communication. OceanX has worked with scientific organisations including Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and NOAA, and with media partners including BBC Studios and National Geographic. It continues to pair research access with films, classroom programmes and fellowships intended to train the next generation of ocean scientists and communicators.

uncertainties: Most current mainstream and canonical sources give Dalio's birth date as 8 August 1949, while the Academy of Achievement gives 1 August, matching the stored record. The day 8 correction is therefore proposed at High rather than Very High confidence.

Dalio founded and built Bridgewater, but he sold his remaining stake and left its board in 2025. Family office principal best captures his current relationship to wealth, while founder remains the durable explanation of how the fortune was created.

Forbes explicitly classifies the fortune as self-made, and multiple profiles positively document a middle-class upbringing, caddie earnings and an apartment-based independent start. Complete family finances are not public, but no inherited business or investment platform is evidenced.

Economic Principles is proposed as the Personal Website because it is Dalio's maintained first-party publishing platform and official social directory. The older raydalio.com domain timed out during review and is not proposed.

Current reporting and 2026 first-party publishing establish that Dalio is living, but mortality status was not changed because the inventory treats only the blank death fields as researchable and no correction is needed to support the biography.
